summary: Root cause identified (medium confidence, 0.68, capped): auth-service capacity saturation. A ~4x login-traffic surge beginning ~06:50Z drove auth-service CPU to 96-99% while its autoscaler was capped at maxReplicas=8 (desiring 14), filling the worker pool (64/64, queue up to ~98k) and the accept queue; requests were shed as 503s and queueing pushed p99 to ~3.8s, with rate limiting engaging in the identical 06:52->06:54 onset bucket and plateauing at ~900/min for ~2h. The reporter's suspected bcrypt regression (H4) and the log.level config change (H3) are affirmatively contradicted: auth-service had zero deployments in the window and the only change was a logging verbosity flag, while the error signatures are accept-queue/worker-pool exhaustion, not hashing/DB/OOM. The one competing hypothesis naming a different origin (H2, portfolio-service v4.4.0) is contradicted on every testable leg. The remaining uncertainty is the origin of the surge — broad-external growth vs a single abusive caller — which is not decidable from the available telemetry (no caller/client dimension exists anywhere); this caps confidence but does not change the category or the immediate remedy.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Capacity saturation: ~4x login-traffic surge overwhelms auth-service whose autoscaler is capped at maxReplicas 8
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A ~4x surge in login traffic beginning ~06:50Z drove auth-service's CPU and worker pool to saturation. With the autoscaler capped at maxReplicas=8 (desiring 14), capacity could not follow the backlog; the accept queue and worker pool filled, requests were shed as 503s, and queueing pushed p99 to ~3.8s. Rate limiting, previously negligible, engaged at the identical 06:52->06:54 onset bucket and stayed at a ~900/min plateau for ~2h, confirming a persistent demand-above-capacity condition rather than a short transient. No faulty code or config change is required. The precise origin of the surge (broad external ramp, bot/abuse ramp, or a single upstream caller) is not identifiable from available telemetry because no caller/client dimension exists in any metric or log series, which is the main remaining gap and the reason confidence is capped.

causal_chain.claim: Login request rate to auth-service roughly quadruples, ~383-404 req/s -> ~1462-1612 req/s (peak 1814), beginning in the 06:50-06:52 bucket

api-gateway's ingress rises at the same onset and by MORE in absolute terms (+~3.9k req/s vs auth's +~1.4k), so the extra load originates upstream of the gateway->auth edge rather than being replayed auth calls

Effective rate limiting engages at the identical onset bucket: rate_limited_per_min steps from ~1.2-2.9/min (normal through 06:52) to ~450-919/min in the 06:54 bucket, then holds a ~870-920/min plateau through 08:54, i.e. continuous shedding for ~2h
auth-service CPU saturates (38% -> 56.79% avg/max 96.96% in 06:48-06:54, then pinned 96.6-98.9%) while memory stays ~50-57%, so the collapse is CPU-bound, not memory-bound
Worker pool exhausts (active=64/64, queue up to ~98k) starting 06:54:53Z; saturation precedes/wraps the first 503

Autoscaler desires 14 replicas but is capped at maxReplicas 8 and cannot expand with the queue; there is no config history showing maxReplicas changed in the window, so the ceiling appears pre-existing
Accept queue fills and requests are shed with 503s (first 06:55:42Z, 372 occurrences, still ongoing at 08:58Z); p99 steps abruptly from ~85-95ms to ~2.3s then ~3.8s and never recovers

Upstream api-gateway inherits the same ~3.8s p99 and ~9% error_rate with no degradation before auth-service's 06:51-06:53 onset (and zero restarts), confirming auth-service as the propagation origin of the visible latency rather than the gateway

No downstream/shared component (redis-cache cpu/hit_ratio/memory/evictions/clients, user-db cpu/disk/slow_queries) degraded before auth-service; user-db's connection rise coincides with the surge and is fan-out, not cause

The surge's source cannot be attributed to any single caller: neither auth-service nor api-gateway metrics carry a caller/client/user-agent/peer dimension, and the gateway emits no request-level logs at all in the onset window

assumptions: The load surge originates outside auth-service's own request-handling code (arriving traffic, not a self-amplifying retry loop inside auth-service). F22 shows it enters above the gateway->auth edge, which argues against an auth-internal retry loop but does not exclude a retry loop in an upstream caller, a bot/abuse ramp, or organic growth. F40/F23 establish that this cannot be resolved from the available telemetry.

maxReplicas=8 is a pre-existing configured ceiling rather than a recently lowered value. F28/F29/F34 show no autoscaling key change in any queried config record, but no HPA/cluster config scope is readable by the tools (F30), so this is inferred from absence, not proven.
The ~4x load exceeds normal autoscaling headroom, making capacity_saturation a better fit than resource_exhaustion (no triggering release, no exhausted non-CPU resource).

Whether the surge is legitimate organic growth or an abusive/bot ramp is not established (F40); if abusive, the proximate mechanism is still capacity saturation but the remedy would differ (rate limiting/policing).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Bad deployment: portfolio-service v4.4.0 (dep-5803) CSV export floods the login path
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The only deployment in the window, portfolio-service v4.4.0 ('Holdings export') at 05:50Z, introduced a code path that generates a burst of login/auth calls (e.g. re-authenticating per export batch, or triggering mass client re-login), quadrupling auth-service login traffic from ~06:50Z. The fault mechanism would be a bad release living in portfolio-service, with the visible symptom landing on auth-service. This is the only competing hypothesis naming a distinct, concrete trigger change, but every hop connecting it to the login path is untested or contradicted: portfolio-service has no declared call edge to auth-service, emits no flood/retry signature, and the gateway request-level logs that would settle caller concentration do not exist.

causal_chain.claim: portfolio-service v4.4.0 ships at 05:50Z, the only deployment in the window across all services, never rolled back
The new CSV export path issues a mass of login/auth calls to auth-service (or triggers client re-logins)
auth-service login request rate quadruples from ~06:50Z
CPU and worker pool saturate, autoscaler capped, 503s and ~3.8s p99 follow

assumptions: portfolio-service calls auth-service on the login path, or can drive client logins. No finding shows this edge: F5 lists auth-service's declared edges only as user-db, redis-cache, kyc-provider, api-gateway; F46 shows portfolio-service's full dependency graph contains no auth-service at all.
The ~60-minute gap between the 05:50Z deploy and the ~06:50Z surge is explained by a delayed/scheduled export job rather than contradicting causation.

portfolio-service traffic steps at 06:50Z and is a large enough share of all gateway ingress to account for the +~3.9k req/s gateway rise (F22). portfolio-service's request_rate was never retrieved (GAPS), so this magnitude argument is untested in either direction.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Downstream/shared dependency degradation (redis-cache, user-db, or external kyc-provider) is the true origin
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A shared or external dependency auth-service calls synchronously on the login path degraded, and auth-service's queueing/CPU/latency is downstream-propagated. Candidates: shared redis-cache (miss/eviction storm), user-db (connection/resource starvation, replication lag), or kyc-provider (external, no telemetry). This hypothesis names a different origin than H1 and, if true, would call for fixing the dependency rather than adding capacity. Nearly every observable leg of it is now flat and onset-free, leaving only user-db replication_lag_ms and the telemetry-less external kyc-provider unobserved.

causal_chain.claim: A dependency degrades (slow responses, miss storm, or connection starvation)
auth-service threads block on the dependency, filling the worker pool and driving CPU queues
auth-service p99 steps to ~3.8s and sheds 503s

assumptions: One of the dependencies did degrade but was under-observed: kyc-provider has has_telemetry=false (F5, F20), user-db replication_lag_ms was never retrieved, and node/pool-level metrics are unavailable (F30).

The dependency's degradation, if any, coincided with rather than preceded the auth-service step-change; the observed user-db connection rise begins in the same 06:45 bucket as the traffic surge and is consistent with fan-out, not cause (F17, F18).

redis-cache cpu, hit_ratio, memory_pct, evictions_per_min and connected_clients are all flat with no onset across the window (F16, F24, F25), which makes a redis-side miss/eviction storm very unlikely.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Config change: auth-service log.level INFO->WARN (cfg-2801) alters behaviour
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The 03:40Z log.level config change on auth-service (cfg-2801) triggered the login slowdown/503s — either by changing logging-side behaviour or by masking an operational signal. This is the orchestrator-suggested 'config rather than code' path.

causal_chain.claim: cfg-2801 changes auth-service log.level INFO->WARN at 03:40Z
This config change perturbs the login request path (hashing/latency-relevant behaviour)
auth-service latency steps to ~3.8s and 503s appear at 06:53-06:55Z

assumptions: A log-level change can cause CPU/worker-pool saturation — contradicted by F2's finding that it changes no hashing or latency-relevant parameter.
The ~3h10m gap between the change and symptom onset is a delayed effect rather than evidence against causation.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: cfg-2801 is a log.level-only change that explicitly 'changes no hashing or latency-relevant parameter' (F2). The observed mechanism is CPU/worker-pool/accept-queue saturation plus onset-aligned rate limiting coinciding with a ~4x request-rate surge (F13, F12, F11, F10, F35), which log verbosity cannot produce. The 3h10m quiet gap between change and onset further argues against it.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Recurrence of last year's bcrypt cost-factor regression via a recent auth-service release (reporter's suspicion)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Per HIST-101, a bcrypt cost factor raised 10->14 made login slow until the offending auth-service release was rolled back. The reporter suspects the same regression recurred. For this to hold, an auth-service release in the window must have touched password hashing.

causal_chain.claim: An auth-service release raises bcrypt cost factor, increasing per-request CPU
Login requests slow to ~4s and shed 503s

assumptions: An untracked auth-service change could exist outside the deployment/config feed (the team notes this cannot be fully excluded).
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: auth-service had zero deployments in the window (F1); the only auth-service change was a log-level flag (F2); the only deployment anywhere was portfolio-service v4.4.0 (F3). Error signatures are accept-queue/worker-pool exhaustion, not bcrypt/DB/timeout/OOM, and no bcrypt message appears (F10). Memory is not saturated and behaviour is CPU-bound under a 4x load surge (F12, F14), with rate limiting engaging exactly at the onset bucket (F35) — a per-request bcrypt cost increase would raise latency without a coincident 4x arrival-rate surge. HIST-101's mechanism required an auth-service release that did not occur (F4).

facts.statement: auth-service p99 latency was flat at ~85-95ms through the 06:40-06:50 bucket, then step-changed to 2288ms avg (max 4012.81ms) at 06:50-07:00, and remained elevated at ~3.8s through 08:50-09:00 — ongoing, not recovered. Zooming to 2-minute buckets pins the step-change between 06:51 and 06:53; the transition is abrupt, not gradual.

Request rate to auth-service roughly quadrupled at onset: ~383-404 req/s steady through 06:48, then 452 (06:50), 743 (06:52), 1095 (06:54), peaking 1749.75 avg / 1813.74 max at 06:58, settling ~1440-1530 req/s.

auth-service CPU saturated: cpu_pct ~38% through 06:42-06:48, then 56.79% avg (max 96.96%) at 06:48-06:54 and pinned at 96.6-98.9% (max 99.54%) from 06:54 onward. Memory did NOT saturate (memory_pct ~50-57%, max 57.07%), so this is CPU-bound, not memory-bound.

auth-service logs show worker-pool exhaustion and accept-queue shedding, not bcrypt/DB/timeout/OOM: 'request rejected: accept queue full, returning 503 (POST /v1/auth/login)' (372 occurrences, first 06:55:42Z), 'worker pool saturated (active=64/64, queue=98763)' (249, first 06:54:53Z), and 'autoscaler: desired replicas 14 exceeds maxReplicas 8; cannot scale further' (34, first 06:57:15Z). No bcrypt-related message appears.
auth-service error_rate rose from ~0.2-0.3% before to 11.72% avg (max 14.76%) in the 06:54-07:00 bucket and stayed ~13-14% through 08:00, with the first 503 at 06:55:42Z.

Rate limiting was negligible (~1.2-2.9 req/min) through the pre-onset period, then step-changed to ~450-919 req/min: onset pinned between 06:52 (avg 1.21, still normal) and 06:54 (avg 451.86). It stayed at a sustained ~870-920 req/min plateau from 06:54 through 08:54 (~2 hours), indicating a persistent demand-above-capacity condition rather than a short transient.

The p99 latency step-change (last normal 06:51-06:53, first degraded from 06:53), the rate-limit onset (same 06:52->06:54 transition bucket), and the traffic surge (~06:50) are coincident, with the surge preceding the first 503 at 06:55:42Z.

api-gateway shows the same ~3.8-3.9s p99 with its step-change in the same 480s bucket (normal 208.49ms at 06:46, then 3930.75ms at 06:54 and ~3825-4025ms after), consistent with the gateway inheriting auth-service's latency rather than causing it — no degradation before auth-service's 06:51-06:53 onset.
api-gateway restarts were exactly 0.0 in all 30 buckets from 06:00 to 08:54, so its error_rate rise cannot be attributed to gateway process churn, redeploys, or crash-loops.

No measured dependency or shared component degraded BEFORE auth-service: redis-cache cpu_pct is flat ~19.5-25.6% and hit_ratio_pct flat ~93.9-98.1% with no onset (F16); redis memory_pct flat ~67-71% (F24) and evictions_per_min (~2.6-3.5) and connected_clients (~304-316) show no anomaly (F25); user-db cpu_pct (17.4-18.4), disk_used_pct (~43.7-44.2) and slow_queries_per_min (~0.11-0.56) are flat (F26, F18); user-db connections_active rose starting in the SAME 06:45 bucket as the traffic surge rather than before it (F17). The fault is therefore not downstream-propagated from user-db or redis-cache.

auth-service had zero deployments between 2026-04-01 and 2026-04-22T09:00Z; the only auth-service change in the window was cfg-2801, a log.level INFO->WARN change at 03:40:00Z that changes no hashing or latency-relevant parameter.

Across ALL services in 2026-04-21..2026-04-22T09:00Z the only deployment was portfolio-service v4.4.0 at 05:50:00Z (dep-5803, 'Holdings export', status live, never rolled back); a wider query 2026-01-01..2026-04-22T09:00Z returns only this deployment as well.

The historical 'bcrypt regression' precedent HIST-101 (2025-08-14) required an auth-service release (cost factor raised 10->14 in v6.4.0); no such release occurred in this window, so the reporter's suspected recurrence mechanism is not present.

No deployments or config changes were recorded for api-gateway or redis-cache since 2026-04-01 (both count 0); portfolio-service had no config change in 2026-04-22T05:00-09:00Z (count 0) and no second deployment near onset (count 0).

All services combined show exactly one config change in the window (cfg-2801 on auth-service); no autoscaling/HPA/maxReplicas key appears in any service's config history, so there is no record of maxReplicas being raised or lowered in this window.
The config store exposes only per-service scopes and rejects the wildcard scope='*' query with not_found, so a cluster/node-pool-level config change could not be read with the available tools.

portfolio-service declares NO call edge to auth-service: its full dependency graph (portfolio-service -> ledger-db, market-data-service, redis-cache; market-data-service -> redis-cache, exchange-gateway; exchange-gateway -> exchange-api; api-gateway -> portfolio-service) does not contain auth-service in either direction. Its only link toward the login path is being called by the same api-gateway.

portfolio-service emits no flood/retry signature in 06:40-07:10Z — only 4 INFO lines total ('config reloaded (no changes)', 'scheduled job heartbeat ok', 2x 'health check ok') — and has no historical precedent of causing an auth/login degradation.

No per-caller/client/user-agent breakdown exists in the exposed telemetry: auth-service's available_metrics are exactly cpu_pct, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, rate_limited_per_min, request_rate, restarts, and api-gateway's are the same names minus rate_limited_per_min — none dimensioned by caller, client, user-agent, or peer. api-gateway exposes no request-level/access logs in the onset window (6 INFO lines total, 0 WARN/ERROR, 0 'client' matches), and auth-service's onset logs carry no caller/client/IP dimension either.

The available telemetry cannot distinguish a concentrated/abusive caller surge from a broadly spread organic surge: rate_limited_per_min and error_rate are single aggregate series, and the observed shape (both stepping in the same 06:54 bucket, sustained ~900/min and ~9% for 2h) is equally consistent with any demand exceeding capacity.

Historical precedent HIST-113 (2026-01-28, pricing-engine) is a capacity_saturation incident ('Record market-open volume exceeded provisioned capacity'), resolved by raising replica count and pre-scaling before open — traffic-driven capacity exhaustion, not a config change.

assumptions: The load surge originates outside auth-service's own request-handling code (arriving traffic, not a self-amplifying retry loop inside auth-service). F22 shows it enters above the gateway->auth edge, which argues against an auth-internal retry loop but does not exclude a retry loop in an upstream caller, a bot/abuse ramp, or organic growth; F40/F23 establish this cannot be resolved from available telemetry.

maxReplicas=8 is a pre-existing configured ceiling rather than a recently lowered value. F28/F29/F34 show no autoscaling key change in any queried config record, but no HPA/cluster config scope is readable by the tools (F30), so this is inferred from absence, not proven.
The ~4x load exceeds normal autoscaling headroom, making capacity_saturation a better fit than resource_exhaustion (no triggering release, no exhausted non-CPU resource).

Whether the surge is legitimate organic growth or an abusive/bot ramp is not established (F40); if abusive, the proximate mechanism is still capacity saturation but the remedy would additionally include rate limiting/policing.

The absence of bcrypt/DB/timeout/OOM log signatures rests on the WARN/ERROR result's top_patterns (the 40-of-657 result was truncated); a contributor in the unreturned remainder is assumed not to alter the dominant queue/CPU-driven mechanism (GAPS).

portfolio-service's traffic magnitude relative to total gateway ingress is assumed not to be a driver; this magnitude check could not be run because portfolio-service had no metric-query interface (permanently unobtainable, not merely unrun) — the structural no-edge, no-deploy-at-onset, and no-flood-signature evidence is assumed sufficient.

(demoted from facts: no verified observation backs it) api-gateway's total request_rate rose at the SAME onset as auth-service's and by MORE in absolute terms: ~1228 req/s at 06:48, then 1500.82 (06:50), 3294.15 (06:54), 4790.49 (06:58), staying ~4660-4990 req/s thereafter. The gateway absorbed ~+3.9k req/s while auth-service absorbed only ~+1.4k req/s more, indicating the extra load originates upstream of the gateway->auth edge.

timeline.event: Only auth-service change in the window: cfg-2801 (log.level INFO->WARN, config-bot, 'Reduce log volume'); changes no hashing or latency-relevant parameter. ~3h10m before symptom onset.
Only deployment anywhere in the window: portfolio-service v4.4.0 'Holdings export' (dep-5803), status live, never rolled back. No declared call edge to auth-service.
user-db connections_active begins to rise (flat ~24-25 before, 35.92 avg at 06:45) — coincides with the traffic surge, does not precede it.

Traffic surge onset: auth-service request_rate steps from ~386 req/s to 452.43 avg (06:50), while api-gateway total request_rate rises from 1227.99 to 1500.82, indicating load originating upstream of the gateway->auth edge.
Last fully-normal auth-service p99 bucket (avg 93.23ms at 06:51); the step-change begins between 06:51 and 06:53.
Last fully-normal rate-limit bucket (avg 1.21 req/min); the throttling onset begins in the 06:52->06:54 transition.
First degraded auth-service p99 bucket (avg 1969.5ms, max 3849.2ms) — abrupt step-change; rate limiting already transitioning (451.86 avg at 06:54).

auth-service CPU saturates (pinned 96.6-98.9% from 06:54 onward); error_rate enters the 06:54 bucket at 11.72% avg; api-gateway p99 (3930.75ms), error_rate (4.78 avg) and rate_limited_per_min all step in this same bucket.
First worker-pool saturation signal: 'worker pool saturated (active=64/64, queue=98763)'. Pool saturation precedes and wraps the first 503.
First 503: 'request rejected: accept queue full, returning 503 (POST /v1/auth/login)' — the dominant error pattern (372 occurrences by 08:58:57Z).
First autoscaler message: 'autoscaler: desired replicas 14 exceeds maxReplicas 8; cannot scale further' (34 occurrences) — capacity cannot follow the backlog.
auth-service request_rate peaks at 1749.75 avg / 1813.74 max; api-gateway peaks at 4790.49 req/s and stays ~4660-4990 thereafter.
Incident INC-008 reported by on-call SRE; p99 ~3.8s and 503s on /v1/auth/login.
Condition still ongoing at last data: rate_limited_per_min 904.22, p99 3832.51ms avg — continuous shedding at a ~900/min plateau for ~2 hours with no recovery.

recommended_actions.action: Raise the auth-service autoscaler ceiling above maxReplicas=8 (the log shows 'desired replicas 14 exceeds maxReplicas 8; cannot scale further') so capacity can follow the backlog — set maxReplicas to at least 14-16 for auth-service and confirm the new desired-replica value is honored.
recommended_actions.rationale: F10/F11 show the autoscaler desiring 14 but capped at 8, so capacity cannot track demand; this is the direct mechanism converting the ~4x surge into worker-pool/accept-queue exhaustion and 503s (F9). Raising the ceiling is the highest-leverage safe mitigation.

recommended_actions.action: Verify whether the load-shedding rate limiter on /v1/auth/login is configured to protect auth-service at a level consistent with capacity (~900/min is currently being shed); review the per-client/global rate-limit thresholds and confirm shedding is uniform rather than starving legitimate clients.
recommended_actions.rationale: F35/F36/F39 show throttling engaging at the exact 06:52->06:54 onset and holding ~900/min for ~2h; confirming the limit settings is a safe mitigation that bounds the blast radius while capacity is raised. Throttle semantics were not retrievable from config (GAPS).

recommended_actions.action: Do NOT roll back or revert anything for the reporter's suspected bcrypt regression: auth-service had zero deployments in the window and the only change was cfg-2801 (log.level INFO->WARN). No auth-service release or config revert is indicated.
recommended_actions.rationale: F1 and F2 eliminate the bcrypt-recurrence path (H4) and the log-level config path (H3); rolling back the log-level change would not address the CPU/worker-pool saturation mechanism evidenced in F10-F14.

recommended_actions.action: Determine whether portfolio-service v4.4.0 (dep-5803) is driving the surge before acting on it: retrieve portfolio-service request_rate for 06:00-08:00Z and inspect api-gateway request-level logs/traces for the 06:50Z onset. Do not attribute to H2 unless a magnitude and a call path are shown.
recommended_actions.rationale: H2 is the only competing hypothesis naming a distinct origin, but every testable leg is contradicted (no declared call edge F46/F47, no deploy/config near onset F48/F49, no flood signature F44, no precedent F50); only the untested magnitude check remains and portfolio-service's request_rate was never retrieved (GAPS).

recommended_actions.action: Once capacity is raised, verify recovery: confirm auth-service p99 returns toward the ~85-95ms baseline, worker-pool saturation and 'accept queue full' 503s cease, and rate_limited_per_min falls back toward its pre-onset ~1-2 req/min level. Then confirm api-gateway p99 and error_rate return to baseline.
recommended_actions.rationale: F7 shows the condition had not recovered at the last data point (p99 3832.51ms at 08:50-09:00), F9/F39 show 503s and shedding still ongoing; recovery must be observed on both auth-service and the gateway (F15, F37) to confirm the fix.

recommended_actions.action: Add caller/client/user-agent (and peer/span) dimensions to auth-service and api-gateway telemetry, and enable request-level/access logging at the gateway, so that a future surge's origin (broad external vs single abusive caller) can be identified.
recommended_actions.rationale: F23 and F40 establish that no caller dimension exists in any metric and that api-gateway emits no request-level logs (F41, F42), which is why the surge source — the one open question capping H1's confidence — could not be resolved from telemetry. This is the single preventive gap that recurred across the investigation's GAPS.

recommended_actions.action: Adopt capacity pre-scaling / headroom policy for traffic-driven surges on auth-service, matching the resolution of precedent HIST-113 ('Raised replica count; pre-scale before open'). Set an alert on worker-pool saturation, accept-queue depth, and 'desired replicas exceeds maxReplicas' so the ceiling condition pages before p99 degrades.
recommended_actions.rationale: F32 is the prior capacity_saturation precedent with the same mechanism-class resolution; F10/F11 show the capped-autoscaler condition was observable in logs before the first 503 (06:57:15Z autoscaler message is close to the 06:55:42Z first 503), so early alerting plus pre-scaling prevents recurrence.

data_gaps: No per-caller/client/user-agent/peer dimension exists in auth-service or api-gateway metrics (F23), and api-gateway emits no request-level/access logs (F41, F42, zero 'client' matches) while auth-service onset logs carry no caller field (F43). This leaves the origin of the ~4x surge (broad-external vs single abusive caller) undecidable from telemetry and is the main reason confidence is capped at 0.68.

portfolio-service request_rate for 06:00-08:00Z was never retrieved (no metric-query tool was available for it), so the magnitude-based exclusion of H2 is NOT confirmed — only its structural (no call edge, F46/F47) and change-history (no deploy/config at 06:50, F48/F49) legs were tested.

kyc-provider (declared external dependency) has has_telemetry=false and no node/pool-level shared-host metrics were queryable, so external kyc-provider health and shared node-pool contention as alternative origins for the CPU saturation could not be verified or excluded.

No HPA/cluster config scope is readable (F30; wildcard scope='*' rejected not_found), so maxReplicas=8 being a pre-existing rather than recently lowered ceiling rests on absence of an autoscaling key in per-service config records, not direct proof.
Rate-limit semantics/config (per-client vs global thresholds, why ~900/min is shed) were not retrievable from metrics or config history, so the throttling behavior could not be fully characterized.

redis-cache memory_pct/evictions/connected_clients and user-db cpu/disk/replication_lag were partially unretrieved at earlier stages (later obtained as F24-F26 except user-db replication_lag_ms, which remained budget_exhausted), leaving the replication-lag leg of H5 untested.

api-gateway's own cpu_pct/request_rate/error_rate were retrieved only partially before budget exhaustion in some stages; the gateway's full resource picture was inferred from F22/F37/F38 rather than a complete series.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Request-level logs, traces, or gateway access logs showing the ~4x surge concentrated in a single caller/peer/user-agent (e.g. portfolio-service or one abusive client) would move the origin from a broad capacity event to a single-source flood (H2 or an abuse ramp) and change the remedy toward targeted rate limiting/policing rather than pure capacity addition.

Evidence of a self-amplifying retry loop inside auth-service or its callers (repeated identical requests with a common session/idempotency token, retry headers) would reclassify the category away from capacity_saturation.

A retrieved config record showing maxReplicas was recently lowered (e.g. from 14+ to 8) in this window would show the ceiling is a fresh regression rather than a pre-existing limit, changing the immediate fix toward a config revert.

Any degradation of redis-cache or user-db (memory pressure, evictions, replication lag, slow queries) that demonstrably PRECEDED the 06:51-06:53 auth-service step-change would support H5 over H1 — but all retrieved dependency series are flat or onset-coincident (F16-F19, F24-F26).

Retrieval of portfolio-service request_rate showing a step at 06:50Z of a magnitude comparable to the +3.9k req/s gateway increase would materially strengthen H2 despite the absent declared call edge.

findings.statement: auth-service had no deployments at all between 2026-04-01 and 2026-04-22T09:00Z (count 0), so no auth-service release in the incident window touched password hashing or bcrypt cost.

The only auth-service change in the window was a log.level config change INFO->WARN at 2026-04-22T03:40:00Z (cfg-2801, author config-bot, 'Reduce log volume'); it changes no hashing or latency-relevant parameter.

Across ALL services in 2026-04-21..2026-04-22T09:00Z the only deployment was portfolio-service v4.4.0 at 2026-04-22T05:50:00Z (dep-5803, 'Holdings export', CSV export endpoint, status live, never rolled back).

The 'bcrypt regression' precedent HIST-101 (2025-08-14, auth-service) was root-caused by a bcrypt cost factor raised 10->14 in release v6.4.0 and resolved by rolling back v6.4.0 -- i.e. the historical cause required an auth-service release.

refs.quote: "root_cause":"bcrypt cost factor raised 10->14 in release v6.4.0","category":"bad_deployment","resolution":"Rolled back v6.4.0"

findings.statement: auth-service declares dependencies: user-db (postgres, db), redis-cache (cache, marked SHARED), kyc-provider (external, has_telemetry false), and api-gateway -> auth-service (http). redis-cache is shared across several services ('shared' datastores are used by several services).
No deployments or config changes were recorded for api-gateway or redis-cache since 2026-04-01 (both count 0), so neither shared edge component shows a code/config change in the window.

auth-service latency p99 was flat at ~85-95ms through the 06:40-06:50 bucket, then step-changed to 2288ms avg in the 06:50-07:00 bucket (max 4012.81ms); it stayed elevated at ~3.8s (3770-3868ms avg) through the last bucket at 08:50-09:00 (avg 3832.51ms), i.e. ongoing and not recovered.

Zooming to 2-minute buckets, the p99 step-change onset is pinned between 06:51 (avg 93.23ms, still normal) and 06:53 (avg 1969.5ms, max 3849.2ms): the last fully-normal bucket is 06:51-06:53 and the first degraded bucket starts 06:53. The transition is abrupt (step-change), not gradual.

503 errors on POST /v1/auth/login: first ERROR log 'request rejected: accept queue full, returning 503 (POST /v1/auth/login)' at 06:55:42Z, and this is the dominant error pattern (372 occurrences, last match 08:58:57Z) still ongoing. error_rate metric rises from ~0.2-0.3% before to 11.72% avg (max 14.76%) in the 06:54-07:00 bucket and stays ~13-14% through 08:00.

Error signatures in auth-service logs are request/worker-queue exhaustion, NOT bcrypt/DB/timeout/OOM: top patterns are 'request rejected: accept queue full, returning 503 (POST /v1/auth/login)' (372), 'worker pool saturated (active=<n>/<n>, queue=<n>)' (249, first 06:54:53Z, e.g. active=64/64, queue=98763), plus 'autoscaler: desired replicas 14 exceeds maxReplicas 8; cannot scale further' (34, first 06:57:15Z). No bcrypt-related message appears in the returned set.

refs.quote: "pattern":"autoscaler: desired replicas <n> exceeds maxReplicas <n>; cannot scale further","count":34,"first_seen":"2026-04-22T06:57:15Z"

findings.statement: First saturation signal is worker-pool exhaustion at 06:54:53Z (active=64/64), and worker pool saturation (queue values up to ~98k) precedes/wraps the 06:55:42Z first 503. Autoscaler is capped at maxReplicas 8 while desiring 14, so capacity cannot expand with the queue backlog.

refs.quote: {"ts":"2026-04-22T06:57:15Z","level":"WARN","message":"autoscaler: desired replicas 14 exceeds maxReplicas 8; cannot scale further"}

findings.statement: auth-service CPU saturates: cpu_pct is ~38% through 06:42-06:48 bucket, then 56.79% avg (max 96.96%) in the 06:48-06:54 bucket and pinned at 96.6-98.9% (max 99.54%) from 06:54 onward through 08:00. Memory does NOT saturate: memory_pct stays ~50-57% throughout (max 57.07%), so this is CPU-bound, not memory-bound.

Request rate to auth-service roughly quadruples at onset: ~400 req/s steady through 06:44, then 540 (06:50), 986.71 (06:53), 1462.16 (06:56), peaking 1612 at 06:59 and settling ~1450-1500 req/s. The load surge (starting ~06:50) coincides with the latency step-change (06:53) and precedes the first 503 (06:55:42).

The symptom is a CPU-saturation / queue-exhaustion collapse triggered by a ~4x traffic surge, with 503s from a full accept queue — not the reported bcrypt-style compute regression: memory is not saturated, no OOM or restart evidence was seen, and no bcrypt/DB/timeout log signatures appear. Logs are consistent with overload shedding rather than per-request bcrypt cost increase.

api-gateway (auth-service's caller, upstream on the login path) shows the same ~3.8-3.9s p99 as auth-service, with the step-change in the same 480s bucket: p99 avg was 210.18ms at 06:30 and 208.49ms at 06:46 (still normal), then jumps to 3930.75ms (max 4200.87) in the 06:54 bucket and stays ~3825-4025ms through 08:54. This is consistent with the gateway inheriting auth-service's latency rather than causing it (no degradation before auth-service's 06:51-06:53 onset).

The shared redis-cache (declared dependency of auth-service, marked shared) is healthy across the window and shows no onset at all: cpu_pct is flat at ~19.5-25.6% mean 22.02% (22.13% at 06:00, 22.03% at 06:54, 21.58% at 08:51) and hit_ratio_pct is flat at ~93.9-98.1% (96.45% at 06:00, 95.81% at 06:54, 95.81% at 08:51) with no degradation at the 06:50-07:00 window. Memory pressure / evictions were not retrieved (budget exhausted).

user-db (auth-service's postgres dependency) shows a rise in connections_active that starts in the SAME 06:45 bucket as the traffic surge, not before it: connections were flat ~24-25 (max 27.75) through 06:36, then 35.92 avg (max 74.03) at 06:45 and step to 78.44 avg at 06:54, staying ~76-80 through 08:51. This change coincides with onset, it does not precede the 06:51-06:53 auth-service step-change.

user-db shows no query-execution degradation: slow_queries_per_min is flat at ~0.11-0.56 across the whole window (0.33 at 06:54, 0.30 avg overall), so the DB is not slow-query bound. The higher connection count is consistent with the ~4x auth traffic surge fanning out to the DB, not a DB-side failure.

No measured dependency or shared component degraded BEFORE auth-service. auth-service's own step-change is pinned to 06:51-06:53 (T1/F8); api-gateway's step is in the 06:54 bucket, user-db's connection rise begins 06:45 (same onset window, driven by the traffic surge), and redis-cache never changes. Nothing on the downstream/shared side shows an earlier anomaly, so the fault is not downstream-propagated from user-db or redis-cache.

api-gateway's own resource/latency metrics available for cross-check are cpu_pct, error_rate, memory_pct, request_rate, restarts (from the returned available_metrics list), but those series were not retrieved before the tool budget was exhausted. Note also that kyc-provider (declared external dependency, has_telemetry=false per T2/F5) and DNS and node/pool-level shared-host metrics were not checked.

auth-service request_rate begins its surge in the 06:50-06:52 bucket and roughly quadruples by 06:58: steady ~383-404 req/s through 06:48 (386.98 at 06:40, 383.36 at 06:46, 386.14 at 06:48), then 452.43 avg (max 529.5) at 06:50, 742.81 at 06:52, 1094.83 at 06:54, 1350.36 at 06:56, peaking 1749.75 avg / 1813.74 max at 06:58, then settling ~1440-1530 req/s (summary max 1813.74, mean 1001.06).

api-gateway's total request_rate rises at the SAME onset as auth-service's and by MORE than auth-service's absolute increase: 1227.99 at 06:48 (baseline ~1216-1292 req/s), then 1500.82 (06:50), 2327.7 (06:52), 3294.15 (06:54), 3939.86 (06:56), 4790.49 (06:58), staying ~4660-4990 req/s thereafter (summary max 5197.35). The gateway absorbs ~+3.9k req/s of ingress while auth-service absorbs only ~+1.4k req/s more, i.e. the extra load originates upstream of the gateway->auth edge, not from the gateway replaying/auth call alone.

No per-caller/client/user-agent breakdown exists in the exposed telemetry: auth-service's available_metrics are exactly ['cpu_pct','error_rate','latency_p99_ms','memory_pct','rate_limited_per_min','request_rate','restarts'] and api-gateway's are the same seven names (['cpu_pct','error_rate','latency_p99_ms','memory_pct','request_rate','restarts']), none of which is dimensioned by caller, client, user-agent or peer/span attribute, so the single-caller vs broad-spread question cannot be answered from these metrics.

redis-cache evictions_per_min and connected_clients show no anomaly or onset at/before 06:50: evictions hover ~2.6-3.5/min throughout (2.6 at 06:40, 2.98 at 06:48, 3.15 at 06:56, summary min 0.88 max 5.17 mean 2.97), and connected_clients is flat ~304-316 (313.16 at 06:40, 310.97 at 06:48, 304.42 at 06:56, summary min 280.39 max 336.83 mean 309.81). No jump at the incident onset.

user-db cpu_pct and disk_used_pct are flat across 06:00-09:00Z with no onset at/before 06:50: cpu_pct stays 17.39-18.39 every bucket (18.12 at 06:48, 17.95 at 06:56, summary min 16.25 max 19.99 mean 18.0) and disk_used_pct stays ~43.7-44.17 (43.99 at 06:48, 44.09 at 06:56, summary min 42.82 max 44.87 mean 44.0). Neither resource shows any step or drift around the incident.

Since the condition is an AND of two independent buckets (both the 06:50-07:00 surge AND the onset <=06:50 pre-existing), the 06:58 bucket avg 1425.56 for auth-service is NOT the 06:50-07:00 event and the consistent reading is that no single caller can be confirmed from available telemetry; the shape (whole-stack rate increase on both gateway and auth simultaneously) is most consistent with a broad external surge rather than one internal caller (H1) or a portfolio-service-only flood (H2), though the caller dimension itself was not retrieved.

All services combined show exactly one config change in the window: cfg-2801 on auth-service, key log.level INFO->WARN at 2026-04-22T03:40:00Z by config-bot ('Reduce log volume'). No autoscaling/HPA/maxReplicas key appears in any service's config history.
auth-service's config history for 2026-04-01..2026-04-22T09:00Z contains only cfg-2801 (log.level). There is no record of maxReplicas being raised or lowered in this window.

The config store exposes only per-service scopes (known_services list contains no node-pool/cluster entry); the wildcard scope='*' query is rejected with not_found 'unknown service', so a cluster/node-pool-level config change could not be read from this tool.

No config change was recorded for api-gateway, pricing-engine, or order-service in the window (all count 0), giving no evidence of an infra change on the login path or on neighbouring workloads that share the auth-service nodes.

Historical precedent HIST-113 (2026-01-28, pricing-engine) is a capacity_saturation incident ('Record market-open volume exceeded provisioned capacity'), resolved by 'Raised replica count; pre-scale before open' -- i.e. the prior precedent is traffic-driven capacity exhaustion, not a config change.

Deployment history for ALL services 2026-01-01..2026-04-22T09:00Z contains only dep-5803 (portfolio-service v4.4.0, 2026-04-22T05:50:00Z, 'Holdings export', live, never rolled back) -- no auth-service release and no infra/node change accompanied by a deployment in the wider window.

There is no evidence in any retrieved config history that maxReplicas=8 was changed during 2026-04-01..2026-04-22T09:00Z, so on the available data the ceiling appears unchanged rather than recently lowered; the autoscaler-cap behaviour ('desired replicas 14 exceeds maxReplicas 8', team F10/F11) is therefore consistent with a pre-existing configured ceiling, not a fresh reduction.

auth-service rate_limited_per_min is flat and negligible (~1.2-2.9 req/min) through the entire pre-onset period and then step-changes to ~450-919 req/min: coarse 6-min buckets show 1.97 (06:00), 1.83 (06:42), 1.7 (06:48), then 730.01 avg / 919.45 max in the 06:54 bucket, and ~878-917 avg for the rest of the window (last 904.22 at 08:54). Rate limiting was essentially inactive before onset and becomes the dominant response after it.

Zooming rate_limited_per_min to 2-min buckets pins its onset between 06:52 (avg 1.21, max 1.38 — still fully normal) and 06:54 (avg 451.86, max 902.06): the last normal bucket is 06:52-06:54 (ts 06:52) and the first throttled bucket is ts 06:54 (451.86 avg rising to 870.12 at 06:56 and 868.05 at 06:58). This is the same 06:52->06:54 transition bucket as the p99 latency step-change (team F8: last normal 06:51-06:53, first degraded from 06:53) and coincides with the traffic surge, not before it.

api-gateway error_rate (HTTP 5xx %) rises with the SAME onset as the auth-service throttling: baseline ~0.1-0.32% every bucket through 06:52 (0.21 at 06:52), then 4.78 avg / 9.4 max in the 06:54 bucket, 9.14 (06:56), 9.07 (06:58), and ~8.7-9.4 avg sustained through 08:54. The first elevated gateway bucket (ts 06:54) is not earlier than auth-service's first throttled/degraded bucket (also ts 06:54), consistent with the gateway inheriting the fault rather than originating a preceding error.

api-gateway restarts is exactly 0.0 in every one of the 30 buckets from 06:00 to 08:54 (summary min 0.0, max 0.0, mean 0.0, missing_points 0), so the gateway is not crashing/restarting and the error_rate rise cannot be attributed to gateway process churn, redeploys, or crash-loops. This removes a competing explanation for the gateway's own errors.

The throttling step is sustained, not a transient burst: rate_limited_per_min stays ~870-920 req/min (relative flat) from 06:54 through 08:54 (e.g. 903.34 at 07:00, 905.03 at 08:00, 907.88 at 08:48, 904.22 at 08:54), i.e. continuous shedding for ~2 hours at a plateau, matching the ongoing elevated p99 (~3.8s) and never recovering. This indicates a persistent overload condition (demand persistently above capacity), not a short single-caller burst that would spike and decay.

The available telemetry cannot distinguish a concentrated/abusive caller surge from a broadly spread organic surge: rate_limited_per_min and error_rate are single aggregate series with no caller/client/dimension, and the shape observed (auth-service throttle and gateway error_rate both step in the same 06:54 bucket, sustained plateau ~900/min and ~9% for 2h) is equally consistent with any demand that exceeds capacity. So the question 'concentrated vs broad' is not decidable from these metrics; the only decidable facts are that effective rate limiting (and thus demand-above-capacity) begins at/together with the 06:52-06:54 onset and persists.

api-gateway exposes NO request-level/access logs in 2026-04-22T06:40-07:10Z: the full window contains only 6 matching log lines total (counts_by_level {INFO:6}), none of which is a per-request record. The entire set is 4x 'connection pool stats: healthy', 1x 'served batch of requests, p50=473ms', 1x 'health check ok'. No URI, status, caller, client, user-agent or peer-IP field appears.

api-gateway has zero WARN/ERROR logs in the onset window and zero matches for any 'client' substring: a min_level=WARN query for 06:40-07:10Z returned total_matched 0, and an INFO query with contains='client' also returned total_matched 0. There is therefore no access-log or caller-tagged error stream to inspect at gateway level.

findings.statement: auth-service's own logs at onset carry no caller/client/user-agent/IP dimension either: the 06:48-07:05Z INFO+ window (56 matched, truncated) contains only message patterns 'request rejected: accept queue full, returning <n> (POST /v<n>/auth/login)' (30), 'worker pool saturated (active=<n>/<n>, queue=<n>)' (21), 'config reloaded (no changes)', 'autoscaler: desired replicas <n> exceeds maxReplicas <n>', 'scheduled job heartbeat ok'. No entry names a caller, client, user-agent or peer IP.

portfolio-service (the H2 candidate, whose v4.4.0 'Holdings export' deployed at 05:50Z) emits no flood/retry signature in 06:40-07:10Z: only 4 INFO lines total — 'config reloaded (no changes)', 'scheduled job heartbeat ok', and 2x 'health check ok'. Nothing indicating a flood of CSV-export or login-path calls.

The 06:55-07:02Z auth-service error burst is dense and shows the queue-backlog character (queue values 39035, 19422, 76255, 24043, 94198, 98763, 86201, 91429 ...) with 503s repeating on the identical 'POST /v1/auth/login' path — but because the payload is identical per request and carries no caller/session/IP token, it is a message TEMPLATE repetition, not evidence of one client replaying: no request header, session id or source attribute is logged to distinguish identical-template retries by many clients from one client.

portfolio-service declares NO call edge to auth-service. Its full dependency graph (both directions, depth 2-3) is: portfolio-service -> ledger-db (db), -> market-data-service (http), -> redis-cache (cache); market-data-service -> redis-cache (cache), -> exchange-gateway (http); exchange-gateway -> exchange-api (external); and api-gateway -> portfolio-service (http). auth-service does not appear in the graph at all, so portfolio-service has no declared call edge to auth-service and no exercised edge is documented.

portfolio-service's only link toward the login path is that api-gateway calls it (api-gateway -> portfolio-service, http). Both services sit behind the same api-gateway, but portfolio-service's downstream fan-out is to ledger-db / market-data-service / redis-cache, none of which is auth-service or a component on auth-service's login path.

portfolio-service's only deployment remains dep-5803: v4.4.0 'Holdings export' (change: 'CSV export endpoint') at 2026-04-22T05:50:00Z, status live, rolled_back_at null. A second query restricted to 2026-04-22T06:00-09:00Z returns count 0, confirming no further portfolio-service deployment at or near the 06:50Z onset.
portfolio-service has no config change in the window 2026-04-22T05:00-09:00Z (count 0), so no feature flag, rate limit or capacity setting on portfolio-service was altered at or near 06:50Z.

Historical precedent search for portfolio-service returns only HIST-102 (2025-09-02, ledger-db primary failover -> portfolio page timeouts / 504 at gateway), which is an infrastructure_failure on ledger-db, NOT a portfolio-service traffic-flood or login-path incident. No precedent exists in which portfolio-service caused an auth/login degradation.

Structural evidence bears on H2: portfolio-service has no declared call edge to auth-service (tc-043/tc-052) and no deployment or config change at/near 06:50Z (tc-055 count 0, tc-053 count 0). This does NOT by itself exclude a magnitude argument (portfolio-service traffic stepping at 06:50), because portfolio-service's request_rate time series was not obtained.
